rule_name: Minimum/maximum wall thickness (ABS)
check_description: Measure nominal wall thickness across all shelled/thin-wall regions of an ABS part and flag regions outside the recommended range.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: Two published ranges differ slightly; treat 1.5 mm as the practical safe minimum for structural ABS parts and 3.5 mm as a soft cap before requiring coring.

rule_name: Minimum/maximum wall thickness (PC)
check_description: Measure nominal wall thickness across a polycarbonate part and flag regions outside the recommended range.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: Consistent with Fictiv's cited PC range of 1.02–3.81 mm.

rule_name: Minimum/maximum wall thickness (PP)
check_description: Measure nominal wall thickness across a polypropylene part and flag regions outside the recommended range.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: Sources disagree on the minimum bound (0.89 mm vs 0.64 mm); use 0.89 mm as the conservative minimum for load-bearing PP features.

rule_name: Minimum/maximum wall thickness (PA / Nylon)
check_description: Measure nominal wall thickness across a nylon (PA6/PA66) part and flag regions outside the recommended range.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: Confirmed by Fictiv's identical cited range. Glass-filled PA grades tolerate thinner sections but need more draft (see Material-Specific rules).

rule_name: Minimum/maximum wall thickness (POM / Acetal)
check_description: Measure nominal wall thickness across a POM (acetal) part and flag regions outside the recommended range.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: POM has high crystallinity and shrinkage; uniform wall thickness matters more here than for amorphous resins (see Warpage rules).

rule_name: Minimum/maximum wall thickness (PBT)
check_description: Measure nominal wall thickness across a PBT part and flag regions outside the recommended range.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide
notes: This published range is notably higher than typical Dyson consumer-part wall sections (often 1.0–3.0 mm for PBT); flagged as questionable — verify against the resin supplier's (e.g. DuPont Crastin, BASF Ultradur) datasheet before using as a hard limit.

rule_name: Minimum/maximum wall thickness (PC/ABS blend)
check_description: Measure nominal wall thickness across a PC/ABS blend part and flag regions outside the recommended range.
typical_threshold: 1.2–3.5 mm (typical, interpolated between PC and ABS)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: No PC/ABS-specific figure was found in the fetched supplier guides; value is interpolated from the individually published PC and ABS ranges and should be verified against the specific blend grade's datasheet (e.g. Covestro Bayblend, SABIC Cycoloy).

rule_name: Uniform wall thickness / adjacent-wall ratio
check_description: Compare wall thickness of adjacent regions across each detected thickness transition; flag transitions where the thinner region is less than 40–60% of the thicker region.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Wall Thickness Design Tips
notes: This is the primary rule used to size ribs, bosses, and gussets relative to nominal wall (see Ribs/Bosses categories).

rule_name: Gradual wall-thickness transition (taper ratio)
check_description: At every location where wall thickness changes, verify the transition is tapered rather than abrupt, with taper length at least 3x the thickness difference.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Abrupt steps concentrate stress and cause sink/warp; the 3x rule-of-thumb is common industry practice but was not found stated numerically in the fetched sources.

rule_name: Minimum draft on all vertical faces
check_description: Check every nominally-vertical face (relative to the assumed pull direction) for a minimum draft angle.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: 0.5° is the absolute floor even for polished, shallow features; most surfaces should carry more (see next rule).

rule_name: Standard draft for typical surfaces
check_description: Check general (non-textured, non-shutoff) vertical/near-vertical faces for the standard recommended draft.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Draft Angle Guidelines / Hubs Injection Molding Guide
notes: Confirmed independently by Hubs ("2° minimum on all vertical walls").

rule_name: Draft scaling with feature depth
check_description: For deep features/pockets, verify draft increases with pull depth per the 1°-per-25 mm (1° per inch) rule of thumb.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Draft Angle Guidelines / Hubs Injection Molding Guide
notes: Hubs phrases the same rule as "+1° per 25 mm"; treat as equivalent.

rule_name: Minimum draft for metal-to-metal shutoffs
check_description: Check faces that form a shutoff (mating steel-on-steel surface, e.g. hole cores through a wall) for minimum draft.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: Below this, shutoff steel wears rapidly and flash risk increases.

rule_name: Additional draft for textured surfaces
check_description: For faces flagged as textured/grained, verify draft meets the texture-depth-dependent minimum.
typical_threshold: 3° (light texture, e.g. PM-T1); 5°+ (heavy texture, e.g. PM-T2)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: See also the finer rule of +1.5° per 0.001 in (0.025 mm) of texture depth under Surface & Cosmetic.

rule_name: Rib draft
check_description: Check the two side faces of every rib for minimum draft.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide / Hubs Injection Molding Guide

rule_name: Boss draft
check_description: Check both the outer and inner (bore) faces of every boss for minimum draft.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide

rule_name: Rib thickness ratio to nominal wall
check_description: At the rib base, measure rib thickness and compare to the thickness of the wall it intersects.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide / Hubs / GD Prototyping
notes: Exceeding this ratio is the single most common cause of visible sink marks opposite ribs.

rule_name: Rib height limit relative to wall thickness
check_description: Measure rib height (from base to tip) and compare to the thickness of the nominal wall it stands on.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide
notes: Hubs states a similar but differently-based limit ("height < 3× rib thickness", i.e. based on the rib's own thickness rather than the nominal wall) — confirm which basis applies before hard-coding a checker threshold.

rule_name: Rib base fillet radius
check_description: Measure the fillet radius at the base of each rib and compare to rib thickness.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide / Hubs Injection Molding Guide
notes: A too-small radius concentrates stress; too-large a radius effectively thickens the rib base and re-triggers the sink-mark rule.

rule_name: Rib spacing from walls and adjacent ribs
check_description: Measure clear spacing between a rib and adjacent ribs or the nearest perpendicular wall.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Hubs Injection Molding Guide
notes: Insufficient spacing causes localized heat/pack buildup between features and can produce localized sink or warp.

rule_name: Rib density / cumulative sink risk
check_description: Assess whether the total ribbed area over a panel is dense enough that cumulative cooling non-uniformity is likely to cause visible surface distortion, even if individual ribs pass thickness/height checks.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Not a single geometric threshold — needs holistic review of rib layout versus part show-surface requirements.

rule_name: Boss outer diameter relative to fastener/insert
check_description: Measure the outer diameter of a boss designed to receive a screw or insert and compare to the fastener's major/insert diameter.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Hubs Injection Molding Guide

rule_name: Boss inner (bore) diameter for self-tapping screws
check_description: Measure the boss bore (pilot hole) diameter and compare to the fastener's core (root) diameter.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Hubs Injection Molding Guide
notes: Undersized bores split the boss on assembly; oversized bores strip.

rule_name: Boss wall thickness relative to nominal wall
check_description: Measure boss wall thickness (the annular wall around the bore, at its base) and compare to the nominal part wall it stands on.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Sink Marks Troubleshooting Guide / GD Prototyping
notes: Same sink-mark mechanism as ribs; ABS-specific guidance (GD Prototyping) cites 40–60%.

rule_name: Boss base fillet radius
check_description: Measure the fillet radius at the base of each boss relative to nominal wall thickness.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Sink Marks Troubleshooting Guide

rule_name: Boss support to main wall
check_description: Check that free-standing bosses (not already attached to a wall) are connected to the nearest wall or panel via a gusset/rib rather than standing unsupported.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Hubs Injection Molding Guide
notes: Unsupported tall bosses are prone to breakage in use and to incomplete fill/packing during moulding.

rule_name: Internal corner radius minimum
check_description: Measure the radius at every internal corner and compare to local wall thickness.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide / GD Prototyping

rule_name: External corner radius sizing
check_description: Measure the radius at every external corner and verify it equals (internal radius + wall thickness), i.e. roughly 1.5× wall thickness when paired with a 0.5×-wall internal radius.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide / Hubs Injection Molding Guide
notes: Keeping external radius = internal radius + wall thickness preserves constant wall thickness around the corner.

rule_name: No unfilleted (sharp) internal corners
check_description: Flag any internal edge with zero or near-zero fillet radius (a true sharp corner) as a stress-concentration and fill/cosmetic defect risk.
typical_threshold: radius > 0 mandatory at all internal corners
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Widely repeated across supplier guides as a general principle but not captured as an explicit numeric line item in the fetched pages.

rule_name: Side-action (slide) maximum width
check_description: For any undercut requiring a side-action/slide, measure the slide's engagement width and compare to the maximum supported by standard tooling.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: This is a Protolabs-published tooling/press limit, not a universal physical law — always confirm against the target manufacturer's press/mould-base size.

rule_name: Side-action (slide) maximum height
check_description: For any undercut requiring a side-action/slide, measure the slide height and compare to the maximum supported by standard tooling.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines

rule_name: Side-action maximum pull distance
check_description: Measure the travel distance the slide/side-action must retract to clear the undercut and compare to the maximum supported pull distance.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines

rule_name: Side-action travel clearance
check_description: Verify the slide/lifter has an unobstructed, perpendicular (typically 90° to the pull direction) travel path with no interference from surrounding geometry, other slides, or the ejector system.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Hubs Injection Molding Guide
notes: Side actions typically add 15–30% to tooling cost per the same source — worth flagging as a cost-relevant design decision, not just feasibility.

rule_name: Undercut ejection via material flex (snap-fits / draftless bumps)
check_description: For shallow undercuts intended to strip directly from the mould (no side action), verify undercut depth stays within the material's safe elastic strain limit for the local wall thickness so the part can flex over the undercut on ejection.
typical_threshold: material- and geometry-dependent; commonly cited ceiling ~5% of hole/undercut diameter for engineering thermoplastics
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Requires material elongation-at-break data plus local geometry, not resolvable from CAD geometry alone; qualitative guidance on flexible-material snap-fits was found (Hubs) but no numeric strain limit was published in the fetched sources.

rule_name: Blind hole depth-to-diameter ratio
check_description: For holes formed by an unsupported core pin from one side only, measure depth and diameter and compute the ratio.
typical_threshold: ?2:1 (unsupported core); higher ratios need core support or become a stepped/tapered core
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Common mould-design rule of thumb; not found stated numerically in the fetched supplier pages.

rule_name: Through-hole depth-to-diameter ratio
check_description: For through-holes formed by cores supported from both sides (or by core + counter-core), measure depth and diameter and compute the ratio.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Common mould-design rule of thumb; not found stated numerically in the fetched supplier pages.

rule_name: Minimum edge distance from hole to part boundary
check_description: Measure the shortest distance from a hole edge to the nearest part edge or intersecting wall.
typical_threshold: ?1× hole diameter, and ?2× local wall thickness
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Prevents thin webs around the hole from short-shotting or cracking; common practice, not found as an explicit numeric line in the fetched sources.

rule_name: Slender core pin support
check_description: Flag small-diameter, deep core pins (forming small-diameter deep holes/blind bosses) that lack adequate depth-to-diameter margin, since they are prone to bending/breaking under injection pressure ("pin push").
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Tooling-side risk flagged qualitatively; ties directly to the blind-hole depth-to-diameter rule above.

rule_name: Hole placement relative to gate / weld-line convergence
check_description: Check whether a hole (which locally displaces flow around a core pin, creating a weld line downstream) sits in a region already flagged as a predicted weld-line convergence zone, compounding a local weak spot.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Weld Lines Troubleshooting Guide
notes: Source discusses weld-line mitigation qualitatively (gate relocation, thinner walls, temperature); no numeric proximity threshold was published.

rule_name: Gate depth as fraction of wall thickness
check_description: Measure gate depth (land thickness) at the gate and compare to the local part wall thickness it feeds, using the appropriate percentage band for the resin's flow characteristics.
typical_threshold: 40–50% (low-viscosity, e.g. PE, nylon); 50–60% (medium-flow); 60–70% (high-viscosity, e.g. acrylic, rigid PVC)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Plastics Technology – Sizing Gates, Runners and Sprues
notes: Use the lower end of the band for thin-walled parts, the higher end for thick-walled parts (need longer pack time).

rule_name: Gate width sizing
check_description: Compute recommended initial gate width from cavity projected area and a material-dependent constant, and compare to the as-designed gate width.
typical_threshold: W = n × sqrt(A) / 30, where n = 0.6–0.9 (material constant), A = cavity area (in²), W in inches
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Plastics Technology – Sizing Gates, Runners and Sprues
notes: Formula is computable from geometry (cavity projected area) but requires a material-constant lookup table per resin family; source explicitly calls the older "width = 2× depth" rule of thumb unreliable.

rule_name: Gate location to control weld-line position
check_description: Check whether the proposed gate location(s) and part geometry are predicted to push resulting weld/knit lines into cosmetically or structurally critical zones, and flag if so.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Weld Lines Troubleshooting Guide
notes: Article gives a worked example (repositioning a gate to move the weld line to a hidden face) but no quantitative rule; true prediction needs mould-flow simulation (see Warpage & Sink category).

rule_name: Balanced / symmetric fill pattern from gate location
check_description: For multi-cavity or geometrically symmetric parts, check that gate placement yields symmetric flow-front travel distances so cavities/features fill and pack evenly.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Standard mould-design principle; not captured with numeric thresholds in the fetched sources.

rule_name: Runner diameter relative to part wall thickness
check_description: Measure runner cross-section (diameter for round/trapezoidal runners) and compare to the thickest downstream part wall it feeds.
typical_threshold: runner diameter typically ? thickest fed wall section, commonly 4–8 mm for general commercial parts
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: General mould-design practice; not found as an explicit numeric rule in the fetched sources — verify against the moulder's own runner-sizing standard.

rule_name: Cold-slug well at runner/sprue junctions
check_description: Check that a cold-slug well (small extension trapping the initially-cooled resin front) is present opposite each sprue/runner junction to prevent cold material from entering the cavity.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Standard tool-design feature; qualitative check only.

rule_name: Ejector pin placement away from cosmetic (Class-A) surfaces
check_description: Flag any predicted ejector-pin contact zone (typically flat, non-cosmetic bosses, ribs, or shut-off pads) that falls on a surface designated as a visible/cosmetic (Class-A) face.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Standard mould-design practice; requires a Class-A/cosmetic-surface tag on the CAD model to check automatically.

rule_name: Ejector pin placement on ribs, bosses, or reinforced pads
check_description: Verify ejector pins are planned to land on structurally robust features (rib tops, boss bottoms, thickened pads) rather than thin, unsupported wall sections.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Ejecting from thin, unsupported walls causes pin push-through, whitening, or deformation.

rule_name: Adequate draft/geometry for ejection force
check_description: For tall ribs/bosses or deep-textured pockets, cross-check that draft and height combine to keep predicted ejection force within a safe margin (i.e. draft satisfies the depth-scaling rule for the feature's actual height).
typical_threshold: flag if feature height exceeds the depth-scaled draft requirement (see Draft category)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Composite check built from the published draft-vs-depth and rib/boss-height rules; true ejection force also depends on material friction coefficient and surface finish, which are not purely geometric.

rule_name: Additional draft for texture depth
check_description: For any face flagged as textured, verify draft includes the extra allowance proportional to texture depth.
typical_threshold: +1.5° per 0.001 in (0.025 mm) of texture depth
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide
notes: Applied on top of the base draft angle for the surface, not in place of it.

rule_name: Minimum embossed lettering height and size
check_description: Measure the raised height and font size of any embossed text/logo feature.
typical_threshold: ?0.5 mm height; ?20 pt equivalent font size
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Hubs Injection Molding Guide
notes: Embossed (raised) text is preferred over engraved (recessed) text as it is cheaper to cut into the mould and more durable in use.

rule_name: Parting line placement away from cosmetic show surfaces
check_description: Check whether the predicted parting line crosses a face designated as a Class-A/show surface, and flag if so.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Requires a Class-A surface tag; standard DFM practice to route parting lines to edges/non-visible transitions.

rule_name: Gate vestige location away from cosmetic show surfaces
check_description: Check whether the planned gate location (and resulting gate vestige/witness mark after trimming) falls on a Class-A/show surface, and flag if so.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Standard DFM practice; requires Class-A surface tagging to automate.

rule_name: Sink mark risk from oversized ribs/bosses
check_description: Flag any rib or boss whose base thickness exceeds 60% of the nominal wall it stands on as a likely visible sink-mark location on the opposite (cosmetic) face.
typical_threshold: flag if rib/boss thickness > 0.6× nominal wall thickness
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Sink Marks Troubleshooting Guide
notes: Directly restates the Ribs/Bosses thickness-ratio rules, applied specifically as a sink-mark predictor.

rule_name: Wall-thickness uniformity as a warpage driver
check_description: Scan the part for regions where adjacent wall thickness ratio falls outside 40–60%, since these thickness steps drive differential cooling/shrinkage and are the leading geometric cause of warpage.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Wall Thickness Design Tips
notes: Same underlying metric as the Wall Thickness category rule, re-applied as a warpage predictor.

rule_name: Flow-length-to-thickness ratio
check_description: Estimate the longest flow path from the (assumed) gate to the farthest fill point, divide by the wall thickness along that path, and compare to the material-specific maximum flow ratio.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide
notes: Geometry gives an approximate flow path, but the true fillable ratio depends on injection pressure, melt temperature, and the specific resin grade's MFI — a full answer needs mould-flow simulation, not geometry alone.

rule_name: Weld-line location and severity prediction
check_description: Predict where flow fronts from multiple gates, around holes, or around obstacles will recombine to form weld/knit lines, and flag those falling in structurally or cosmetically critical zones.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Weld Lines Troubleshooting Guide
notes: Source confirms this is normally addressed via gate relocation, process tuning (temperature/speed/pressure), or mould-flow simulation rather than a simple geometric formula.

rule_name: Cooling balance around ribs, bosses, and thick sections
check_description: Check for the presence/feasibility of cooling channels close and parallel to thick sections, ribs, and bosses, since uneven core-vs-cavity cooling is a major warpage driver independent of wall thickness alone.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: A geometric checker can only assess proxy signals (thick-section clustering, rib/boss density); actual cooling-line layout is a tooling decision outside the part CAD.

rule_name: Anisotropic shrinkage/warp risk for fibre-filled grades
check_description: For parts specified in glass- or mineral-filled resin grades, flag long, flat, unsupported panels as higher warp risk due to differential shrinkage parallel vs. perpendicular to fibre/flow orientation.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Well-established polymer-processing effect; not captured numerically in the fetched supplier design-guide pages, so treated as LLM knowledge pending a dedicated material-supplier source.

rule_name: Standard (commercial) linear dimensional tolerance
check_description: For dimensions not explicitly called out as critical/precision, compare achieved tolerance against the standard commercial-grade band for the feature size.
typical_threshold: ?±0.1 to ±0.25 mm for typical consumer-product feature sizes (size-dependent; grows for larger features)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Tolerances Guide / Protolabs Injection Molding Design Guidelines
notes: Protolabs states a resin/machining base of ±0.08 mm plus an added resin tolerance not falling below ±0.002 in/in; Fictiv gives ±0.1 mm as typical for non-critical dimensions, tightening to ±0.025 mm for medical-grade work.

rule_name: Fine/precision tolerance capability
check_description: For dimensions explicitly flagged as critical/precision, compare achieved tolerance against the tighter precision-grade band, noting the associated cost/complexity premium.
typical_threshold: down to ?±0.125 mm feasible with cost premium; ?±0.025 mm achievable for the tightest features with secondary operations
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Design Guide
notes: Runs under ~10,000 units often need secondary (machining) operations to reliably hit the tightest bands.

rule_name: Additional tolerance allowance across parting lines
check_description: For any dimension that spans the mould parting line, verify an additional tolerance allowance has been applied beyond the standard single-cavity-side tolerance.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Tolerances Guide
notes: Source explicitly states dimensions measured across a parting line cannot be held to the same precision as same-side dimensions, due to mould half alignment/wear.

rule_name: Hole diameter tolerance by size band
check_description: For moulded (not drilled/reamed) holes, compare achieved diameter tolerance to the size-dependent commercial band.
typical_threshold: ?±0.05–0.15 mm across the 0.3–40 mm bore range (commercial grade)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Tolerances Guide

rule_name: Flatness/straightness tolerance
check_description: For nominally flat panels, compare measured flatness deviation to the size- and material-dependent commercial band.
typical_threshold: ?0.3–0.85 mm depending on material and span (0–160 mm range cited)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv Injection Molding Tolerances Guide
notes: Flatness is strongly linked to warpage risk (see Warpage & Sink category) rather than being purely a moulding-precision issue.

rule_name: ABS mould shrinkage rate
check_description: Use as an input to scaling/tolerance checks and as a cross-reference when evaluating wall-thickness/warp rules for ABS parts.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Standard published resin-grade value range from general polymer processing knowledge; not confirmed against a specific fetched supplier datasheet in this pass.

rule_name: PC mould shrinkage rate
check_description: Use as an input to scaling/tolerance checks for polycarbonate parts.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: General polymer processing knowledge; not confirmed against a specific fetched supplier datasheet in this pass.

rule_name: PP mould shrinkage rate (high, warp-prone)
check_description: Flag PP parts for closer scrutiny of the wall-uniformity and cooling-balance warpage rules, since PP's semi-crystalline structure gives it markedly higher and more anisotropic shrinkage than amorphous resins like ABS/PC.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: General polymer processing knowledge; not confirmed against a specific fetched supplier datasheet in this pass. Directional (flow vs. cross-flow) shrinkage differential is the key warp driver for PP.

rule_name: PA66 (Nylon) mould shrinkage rate and moisture sensitivity
check_description: Flag PA parts for post-mould dimensional-stability review, since PA66 shrinkage is both high and moisture-dependent (parts continue to change dimension as they absorb ambient moisture after moulding).
typical_threshold: 0.5–2.5% (unfilled; lower for glass-filled grades), plus post-mould moisture-driven growth
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: General polymer processing knowledge; not confirmed against a specific fetched supplier datasheet in this pass.

rule_name: POM (Acetal) mould shrinkage rate (high, warp-prone)
check_description: Flag POM parts for closer scrutiny of the wall-uniformity and cooling-balance warpage rules, since POM's high crystallinity gives it high shrinkage and strong sensitivity to wall-thickness non-uniformity.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: General polymer processing knowledge; not confirmed against a specific fetched supplier datasheet in this pass.

rule_name: PBT mould shrinkage rate
check_description: Use as an input to scaling/tolerance checks and warp risk review for PBT parts.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: General polymer processing knowledge; not confirmed against a specific fetched supplier datasheet in this pass; see also the flagged wall-thickness range disagreement for PBT in the Wall Thickness category.

rule_name: Increased draft for glass/mineral-filled grades
check_description: For parts specified in a glass- or mineral-filled resin grade, verify draft angles are increased (typically +1° over the unfilled-resin baseline) to account for higher shrinkage onto cores and increased mould-wall friction/abrasiveness.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (supplier design guides) — no ISO equivalent
notes: Standard filled-resin moulding practice; not found as an explicit numeric line item in the fetched supplier pages during this pass — verify against the specific filled grade's processing guide.

rule_name: Minimum wall thickness by alloy and panel area
check_description: Measure the thinnest wall region on the part and compare against the minimum allowable thickness for the alloy family, scaled by the local panel surface area.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: CASTMOLD Die Casting Part Design 14 Principles
notes: Aluminum/magnesium vs zinc thresholds differ; scales with panel area, not a single flat value.

rule_name: Recommended (target) wall thickness by alloy and panel area
check_description: Compare average wall thickness in each panel region to the recommended (not just minimum) thickness band for the alloy and panel size to flag under- or over-designed sections.
typical_threshold: Al/Mg: 2.0-3.5mm; Zinc: 1.5-2.5mm depending on panel area
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: CASTMOLD Die Casting Part Design 14 Principles
notes: Recommended band, not a hard pass/fail minimum.

rule_name: Maximum thick-to-thin wall ratio
check_description: Identify adjacent wall regions and compute the ratio of thickest to thinnest connected sections; flag ratios exceeding the recommended maximum to avoid sink and porosity risk.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: CASTMOLD Die Casting Part Design 14 Principles

rule_name: Overall wall thickness upper bound
check_description: Flag any solid wall section exceeding the general practical maximum thickness for die castings, since thick sections increase cycle time and porosity risk.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: CASTMOLD Die Casting Part Design 14 Principles
notes: General guidance; alloy- and part-specific exceptions exist.

rule_name: Minimum draft angle on internal (core) surfaces by alloy
check_description: Measure draft angle on faces parallel to the die-pull direction and flag internal/core surfaces below the alloy-specific minimum draft.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: CASTMOLD Die Casting Part Design 14 Principles
notes: Zinc allows the least draft (best flow), aluminum needs more due to higher shrinkage/friction.

rule_name: Outer surface draft double the internal draft
check_description: Compare draft angle on external (cosmetic) surfaces to internal surfaces on the same part and flag external draft below roughly twice the internal minimum.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: CASTMOLD Die Casting Part Design 14 Principles

rule_name: Deep feature draft escalation
check_description: For deep pockets, windows, or bosses (e.g. >50mm draw depth), verify draft angle increases beyond the base minimum to reduce ejection sticking risk.
typical_threshold: 3-4 (deep features ~50mm depth); base ejector zones >=0.5, deep windows 2-3
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Pro Die Casting Design Tips
notes: Values reflect general vendor guidance, not a single standards body.

rule_name: Lettering/logo minimum draft
check_description: Check raised or recessed lettering/logo features for draft angle at or above the high minimum required for legible, releasable text.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: NADCA Product Specification Standards for Die Castings (Section 6, Additional Specification Guidelines)

rule_name: Rib base thickness relative to wall
check_description: Measure rib base thickness at its attachment to the parent wall and compare to the recommended fraction of nominal wall thickness to avoid sink marks and heat trapping.
typical_threshold: 0.5-0.7x wall thickness (some sources cite up to 1x)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Pro Die Casting Design Tips
notes: CASTMOLD source states 0.6-1.0x T; ranges vary by source, use as advisory band.

rule_name: Maximum rib height relative to thickness
check_description: Measure rib height from its base and flag ribs exceeding the maximum multiple of rib thickness, which risk mis-fill or reduced stiffening benefit.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: CASTMOLD Die Casting Part Design 14 Principles

rule_name: Minimum rib-to-rib spacing
check_description: Measure center-to-center or clear spacing between parallel ribs and flag spacing below the recommended multiple of rib thickness to prevent localized heat buildup.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Pro Die Casting Design Tips

rule_name: Internal fillet radius at wall junctions (NADCA tee/cross formulas)
check_description: At tee, cross, and Y-shaped wall intersections, measure the internal fillet radius and compare against the NADCA formula based on adjoining wall thickness(es).
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: NADCA Product Specification Standards for Die Castings (Section 6, Additional Specification Guidelines)
notes: T1/T2 = adjoining wall thicknesses; formula from NADCA product specification guidance, not a dimensional/GD&T ISO standard.

rule_name: Minimum internal corner radius (general)
check_description: Scan for internal edges/corners below the minimum radius threshold, which increase die wear and stress concentration.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Pro Die Casting Design Tips
notes: Sharp internal radii <0.25mm reported to increase die wear up to ~30%.

rule_name: External corner radius minimum
check_description: Check external (outside) corners for a minimum radius to avoid stress risers and casting cracking at sharp edges.
typical_threshold: >=1.0mm (internal radius + wall thickness, per NADCA-derived guidance)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Pro Die Casting Design Tips

rule_name: Flag undercuts requiring core pulls/slides
check_description: Detect geometry with features perpendicular to the primary die-draw direction that cannot release without a side-action slide or core, and flag for tooling complexity/cost review.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Pro Die Casting Design Tips
notes: No numeric threshold published; presence/absence and orientation relative to draw direction is the checkable condition.

rule_name: Parting line placement away from cosmetic (Class A) surfaces
check_description: Verify the detected/assumed parting line does not cross designated cosmetic or high-wear surfaces; flag if it does.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Pro Die Casting Design Tips

rule_name: Ejector pin witness mark depth tolerance
check_description: Where ejector pin locations are known/inferred (typically flat, non-cosmetic faces), check that resulting raised/depressed witness marks stay within the published tolerance.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: NADCA Product Specification Standards for Die Castings (Section 6, Additional Specification Guidelines)

rule_name: Minimum ejector pin pad diameter relative to pin
check_description: Where ejector locations are inferred on flat non-cosmetic bosses, check that the surrounding land/pad diameter is at least the recommended multiple of pin diameter to prevent punch-through.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Pro Die Casting Design Tips
notes: Requires knowledge of actual ejector pin layout, which is a tooling design decision not always derivable from part CAD alone.

rule_name: Flow-path length to wall thickness ratio (filling turbulence risk)
check_description: Estimate the longest metal flow path from a plausible gate location to the farthest extremity relative to local wall thickness; flag high ratios as at risk of incomplete fill/turbulent flow.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: NADCA-derived practice via Dynacast/Xometry design guidance (no single explicit ratio published in fetched sources)
notes: Fetched public sources reference flow-length risk qualitatively (thin walls 1.5-2.5mm risk short shots) but do not publish a single numeric flow-length:thickness limit; actual gate location is a tooling decision not derivable from CAD alone, hence not-yet-computable.

rule_name: Thick-section porosity / hot-spot risk from mass concentration
check_description: Compute local thermal modulus (volume/surface-area) across the part and flag isolated thick masses or poorly-cored bosses that will solidify last and trap shrinkage porosity.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: NADCA Product Specification Standards for Die Castings (Section 6, Additional Specification Guidelines)
notes: NADCA notes thin walls are largely free of porosity while thick walls retain internal porosity; use coring to break up mass concentrations.

rule_name: Pressure-tightness capability check for sealed cavities
check_description: For parts with sealed/pressurized functional cavities, flag against typical achievable pressure-tightness ratings for die castings, since standard die castings are not inherently leak-tight.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: NADCA Product Specification Standards for Die Castings (Section 6, Additional Specification Guidelines)
notes: Requires functional/sealing requirement input beyond pure geometry; flag for manual review when cavity is detected.

rule_name: Hole depth-to-diameter (as-cast) aspect ratio limit
check_description: Measure the depth-to-diameter ratio of cored holes and compare against the alloy-specific as-cast economical and technical limits; deeper holes require secondary drilling.
typical_threshold: Economical 4-6d; technical limit 8-12d (general); alloy-specific: Al<=4:1, Zn<=5:1, Mg<=3:1
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: CASTMOLD Die Casting Part Design 14 Principles; Xometry Pro Die Casting Design Tips
notes: Two fetched sources give slightly different alloy-specific figures; treat as advisory ranges.

rule_name: Optimum nominal wall thickness range
check_description: Measure nominal wall thickness across the part and flag regions outside the optimum published range for consistent feedstock filling and predictable sintering shrinkage.
typical_threshold: 1-6mm (0.040-0.120in typical; up to 0.5in with cost/cycle penalty)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: MIM Design Guide (facfox.com PDF)
notes: Localized minimum down to 0.25mm (0.010in) possible but not across an extended span.

rule_name: Absolute minimum wall thickness (localized)
check_description: Flag any wall region below the absolute minimum thickness achievable in MIM feedstock filling, which risks short shot and distortion even if localized.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Machine Design - Design Considerations for Metal Injection Molding
notes: Different sources cite 0.005in vs 0.010in minimum; use as advisory lower bound, distortion risk noted at the extreme.

rule_name: Maximum practical wall thickness
check_description: Flag wall sections exceeding the practical maximum thickness, since thicker MIM sections greatly increase debind/sinter cycle time and risk internal defects.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Advanced Powder Products MIM Design Guide

rule_name: Powder flow restriction from thin-wall / long-flow-path combination
check_description: Identify thin-wall regions combined with long flow distance from the gate; flag as at risk of powder/binder feedstock flow restriction leading to incomplete filling.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: MIM Design Guide (facfox.com PDF)
notes: No single published numeric flow-length:thickness ratio for MIM found in fetched sources; gate location is a tooling decision not derivable from CAD alone.

rule_name: Rib thickness relative to adjoining wall
check_description: Measure rib thickness at its base and compare against the recommended fraction of the adjoining wall thickness to reduce sink marks and binder/powder segregation.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: MIM Design Guide (facfox.com PDF)
notes: Machine Design source states rib thickness should not exceed the adjoining wall thickness (i.e. <=1x); facfox gives ~0.75x; use 0.75x as tighter/preferred target.

rule_name: Gradual wall thickness transition (avoid abrupt steps)
check_description: Scan for abrupt step changes between adjoining wall thicknesses and flag transitions lacking a gradual taper/blend, which risk binder-powder separation and sink at the step.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: MIM Design Guide (facfox.com PDF)
notes: Abrupt transitions are cited as a mechanism for binder separation and short shot.

rule_name: Minimum fillet/corner-break radius
check_description: Scan for sharp (zero-radius) internal and external corners and flag any below the minimum published break radius, since sharp corners impede feedstock flow and act as crack initiation sites after sintering.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: MIM Design Guide (facfox.com PDF)
notes: Sharp corners are a documented stress-concentration/crack-initiation risk during sintering shrinkage.

rule_name: Draft angle on tall internal features
check_description: Check draft angle on deep internal walls/core pins; MIM generally needs little to no draft on shallow features but slight taper is recommended as depth increases to ease green-part ejection.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Machine Design - Design Considerations for Metal Injection Molding
notes: facfox source states most MIM parts do not require draft; treat 0.25-0.5deg as a guideline for deeper features only.

rule_name: Undercut/side-action demoulding feasibility flag
check_description: Detect geometry features perpendicular to the primary mould-pull direction (e.g. side holes, snap features) that require a side-action or lifter, and flag for tooling complexity review.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Advanced Powder Products MIM Design Guide
notes: Guide recommends orienting features perpendicular to the parting line for ejection; undercuts require slides/lifters similar to plastic injection moulding.

rule_name: Linear sintering shrinkage allowance
check_description: Verify the CAD 'green' (pre-sinter) model has been scaled up by the material-specific linear shrinkage factor so the as-sintered part meets nominal dimensions.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Machine Design - Design Considerations for Metal Injection Molding; MIM Design Guide (facfox.com PDF)
notes: Shrinkage is material (feedstock/binder system) dependent; must be uniform/isotropic or distortion results.

rule_name: Non-uniform mass distribution causing anisotropic sintering distortion
check_description: Compute mass/volume distribution asymmetry across the part and flag regions where uneven wall thickness or mass concentration will shrink at different rates during sintering, causing warpage.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Machine Design - Design Considerations for Metal Injection Molding
notes: Uniform wall thickness is repeatedly cited as the primary lever to control distortion; direct link to MIM-006.

rule_name: As-sintered dimensional tolerance capability
check_description: Compare specified dimensional tolerances on the drawing/model against the typical as-sintered capability; flag tolerances tighter than achievable without secondary machining.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Machine Design - Design Considerations for Metal Injection Molding; MIM Design Guide (facfox.com PDF)
notes: facfox cites +/-0.3%; Machine Design cites +/-0.3-0.5%; use the tighter figure as the pass threshold and flag anything requiring better.

rule_name: Minimum as-sintered relative density
check_description: Where density-dependent mechanical properties are required, flag part regions/features whose expected sintered density falls below the typical achievable range, indicating residual porosity/short-shot risk.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Advanced Powder Products MIM Design Guide; Machine Design
notes: Density is a material/process outcome, not directly measurable from CAD geometry alone; flag geometry (thick sections, poor flow paths) known to correlate with lower density.

rule_name: Feature requiring secondary machining beyond as-sintered tolerance
check_description: Flag any dimension or surface finish callout tighter than as-sintered MIM capability (tolerance or Ra) as requiring a secondary machining, tumbling, or plating operation.
typical_threshold: As-sintered Ra ~32 microinch; secondary ops needed below ~16 microinch
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: MIM Design Guide (facfox.com PDF)

rule_name: Stress concentration flag at unfilleted rib/wall junctions
check_description: Detect rib-to-wall or wall-to-wall junctions lacking a blending fillet and flag as stress concentration / crack initiation sites, particularly relevant given post-sinter shrinkage stresses.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Machine Design - Design Considerations for Metal Injection Molding

rule_name: Minimum practical wall thickness
check_description: Measure minimum wall thickness on features perpendicular to the pressing axis and flag walls thinner than the practical minimum, which risk tooling fragility and inconsistent fill.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Powder Metallurgy Part Design Guide (powdermetallurgy.com)
notes: Atlas Pressed Metals independently confirms 0.060in (1.52mm) minimum.

rule_name: Straight-through walls require no draft
check_description: Confirm walls parallel to the press/ejection direction (straight-through bores/OD) are not flagged for missing draft, since PM parts are compacted and ejected in a straight line and do not need draft on primary walls.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Atlas Pressed Metals Powder Metallurgy Design Tips
notes: This differentiates PM from die casting/MIM/injection moulding, where draft is normally mandatory.

rule_name: Boss and flange sidewall draft for ejection
check_description: Measure draft angle on boss sidewalls, flange steps, and counterbore walls (features not aligned with straight pressing direction release) and flag values below the recommended minimum.
typical_threshold: 7-15 (sources range 7-15 deg; one source cites >=12 deg minimum each side)
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Powder Metallurgy Part Design Guide (powdermetallurgy.com); Atlas Pressed Metals Powder Metallurgy Design Tips
notes: Two fetched sources disagree on exact figure (7-15deg vs >=12deg); treat as advisory band, not single fixed value.

rule_name: No undercuts or transverse (cross) holes in press direction
check_description: Detect any undercut or hole with axis transverse to the pressing direction; these cannot be formed directly by uniaxial compaction and must be flagged as requiring secondary machining or a redesigned press axis.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Powder Metallurgy Part Design Guide (powdermetallurgy.com)
notes: Fundamental process constraint of uniaxial pressing; distinguishes PM from casting/MIM which can use side-action tooling.

rule_name: Maximum length/height-to-diameter aspect ratio
check_description: Compute the ratio of pressing-direction height to smallest cross-sectional dimension and flag parts exceeding the maximum practical aspect ratio, which causes density gradients along the fill depth.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Powder Metallurgy Part Design Guide (powdermetallurgy.com)
notes: Also bounded by absolute size caps (diameter <=250mm, height <=200mm) per same source.

rule_name: Prefer chamfers over radii at tool-wear-prone edges
check_description: Scan sharp edges at the punch/die interface and flag radiused corners where a chamfer (30 or 45 degrees) with a defined flat would be preferred for tooling durability, per PM tooling practice.
typical_threshold: 30 or 45 degree chamfer preferred; minimum flat land 0.13mm
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Powder Metallurgy Part Design Guide (powdermetallurgy.com)
notes: Radii create thin, fragile tool steel sections at the punch tip; chamfers are more robust for high-volume tooling.

rule_name: Minimum countersink flat
check_description: Check countersunk features for a minimum flat land before the taper begins, to avoid a feather-edge on the compaction punch.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Atlas Pressed Metals Powder Metallurgy Design Tips

rule_name: Minimum land at taper-to-die-wall transition
check_description: Check tapered wall sections for a minimum straight land between the taper and the die wall, required to prevent a fragile feather edge on the die/punch.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Powder Metallurgy Part Design Guide (powdermetallurgy.com)

rule_name: Maximum groove depth relative to part length
check_description: Measure groove depth (curved/semicircular vs rectangular profile) and flag against the maximum depth fraction of overall part length, beyond which powder fill and tool strength become unreliable.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Powder Metallurgy Part Design Guide (powdermetallurgy.com)

rule_name: Sintering linear dimensional change allowance
check_description: Verify the green (pre-sinter) compact dimensions account for the expected linear dimensional change during sintering so the finished part meets nominal drawing dimensions.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Sinterworks DFM Guide for Powder Metallurgy
notes: PM shrinkage is much smaller than MIM (0.5-1.5% vs 14-22%) because PM parts are pressed near-final size; can be growth or shrinkage depending on alloy/copper content.

rule_name: Density gradient risk from non-uniform cross-section
check_description: Identify non-uniform cross-sections (varying thickness at the same press-depth level) and flag as at risk of density gradients that cause differential sintering shrinkage and warpage.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Sinterworks DFM Guide for Powder Metallurgy
notes: Uneven density from non-uniform fill depth is the primary distortion driver in press-and-sinter PM.

rule_name: Practical as-pressed/sintered dimensional tolerance by feature type
check_description: Compare specified tolerances for diameters, press-direction length, concentricity, and flatness/parallelism against the typical achievable PM tolerance for each feature type; flag tolerances tighter than standard capability as requiring sizing or machining.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (industry design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Powder Metallurgy Part Design Guide (powdermetallurgy.com)
notes: Length in the pressing direction is much tighter (held by tooling) than radial dimensions (governed by die/sintering); direction-dependence should be tracked by the checker.

rule_name: Minimum inside bend radius >= material thickness
check_description: For each bend feature, verify the inside bend radius is at least equal to the sheet material thickness T, to avoid excessive thinning and cracking at the bend.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guide
notes: General guideline across steel, aluminium, stainless; brittle tempers (e.g. 6061-T6) need a larger radius, see SM-004.

rule_name: Bend radius within standard tooling range
check_description: Check that specified internal bend radii fall within the standard press-brake tooling range so no custom tooling is required.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs: The Basics of Bend Radii in Sheet Metal
notes: Standard tooling increments in 0.01in steps; radii outside range increase cost/lead time.

rule_name: Default bend radius recommendation
check_description: Flag bend features that do not use the shop default radius (~0.76 mm / 0.030 in), which is manufacturable on roughly 95% of parts without special tooling.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs: The Basics of Bend Radii in Sheet Metal

rule_name: Larger bend radius required for crack-prone aluminium tempers
check_description: For parts in brittle tempers such as 6061-T6 aluminium, verify bend radius is increased beyond the standard minimum to prevent cracking at the bend line.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs: The Basics of Bend Radii in Sheet Metal
notes: Material dependence: called out specifically for 6061-T6 aluminium; mild steel/stainless are less prone to bend cracking.

rule_name: Minimum bend relief width
check_description: At each bend that terminates before a part edge, verify the relief notch width is at least half the material thickness, to prevent uncontrolled tearing beyond the bend line.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: SendCutSend: How to Design Bend Reliefs & Corner Reliefs for Sheet Metal Parts

rule_name: Minimum bend relief depth
check_description: Verify relief cut depth, measured from the bend line into the flat, is at least material thickness plus bend radius plus about 0.5 mm, giving material room to deform without tearing.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: SendCutSend: How to Design Bend Reliefs & Corner Reliefs for Sheet Metal Parts

rule_name: Minimum gap between adjoining flanges at corner reliefs
check_description: Where two bends meet at a corner, check that the gap left between the resulting flanges is at least 0.4 mm to avoid flange collision/interference after forming.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: SendCutSend: How to Design Bend Reliefs & Corner Reliefs for Sheet Metal Parts

rule_name: Relief feature required wherever a bend line meets an edge or cutout
check_description: Check that every bend line intersecting an edge, hole, or flange boundary has a relief feature (rectangular, obround, or round) present rather than a sharp corner, to prevent stress-concentration tearing.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guidelines

rule_name: Minimum hole-to-bend distance
check_description: For any hole or slot near a bend, verify the distance from the hole edge to the start of the bend radius is at least 4x material thickness, to avoid hole distortion during forming.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs: The Basics of Bend Radii in Sheet Metal

rule_name: Minimum hole-to-edge distance
check_description: Check that every hole's edge clearance to the nearest sheared/cut part edge is at least one material thickness, to prevent edge tear-out.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guide

rule_name: Minimum hole-to-hole spacing
check_description: For pairs of holes/slots, verify centre-to-centre spacing leaves at least 2x material thickness of web between features, to preserve web strength.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guide

rule_name: Minimum hole diameter relative to thickness
check_description: Flag holes with diameter smaller than the sheet thickness, since punched/cut holes below this ratio risk poor roundness or tool breakage.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guidelines

rule_name: Minimum notch width and max length-to-width ratio
check_description: Check narrow notch cutouts have width at least material thickness (or 1 mm, whichever is larger) with overall length no more than 5x that width, to avoid tool/die breakage or notch collapse.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guidelines
notes: Max length = 5x width.

rule_name: Minimum tab width and max length-to-width ratio
check_description: For protruding tabs, verify width is at least 2x material thickness (or 3.2 mm, whichever is larger) with length no more than 5x width, to prevent bending/breaking during handling.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guidelines
notes: Max length = 5x width.

rule_name: Minimum flange length
check_description: For each flange adjacent to a bend, verify its flat length beyond the bend tangent line is at least 4x material thickness, so it can be reliably clamped and formed.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guidelines

rule_name: Minimum flange height including bend radius
check_description: Check flange height, from base surface to flange tip, is at least twice the material thickness plus the bend radius, the practical minimum the press brake can reliably form.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guide

rule_name: Minimum hem return length
check_description: For hemmed edges (folded-back flanges), verify the returned flange length is at least 6x material thickness and the hem's inside gap is at least one material thickness, so the hem closes without cracking.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guidelines

rule_name: K-factor within typical bend-allowance range
check_description: When unfolding the flat pattern, verify the K-factor used for bend allowance/deduction calculation falls within the typical 0.3-0.5 range appropriate to the bend method (air bend vs. bottom bend) and material.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guide
notes: Air bend ~0.33, bottom/coin bend ~0.42, large radii approach 0.5; varies by material and process.

rule_name: Kerf compensation applied to flat pattern outline
check_description: Verify the flat-pattern outline accounts for cutting kerf (approx. 0.15 mm added/removed per side) so mating/nested features meet nominal dimensions after cutting.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guide
notes: Laser kerf ~0.3mm total width; plasma/waterjet kerf differs and needs process-specific compensation.

rule_name: Draw ratio limit per draw operation
check_description: For deep-drawn features, compute the draw ratio (blank diameter divided by punch diameter) and flag values above about 2.0, which typically require multiple draw stages to avoid tearing.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Wikipedia: Rule-based DFM analysis for deep drawing
notes: Requires blank-to-punch diameter extraction from a formed feature; not derivable from bend-line geometry alone.

rule_name: Die corner radius relative to sheet thickness
check_description: For deep-drawn parts, verify the die-entry corner radius is 5-10x sheet thickness, to minimise wrinkling and cracking as material is drawn into the cavity.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Wikipedia: Rule-based DFM analysis for deep drawing
notes: Applies to drawn/formed cavity features, not simple press-brake bends.

rule_name: Punch corner radius relative to sheet thickness
check_description: Check that punch corner radius on deep-drawn features is 4-10x sheet thickness, to prevent cracking at the point of maximum thinning near the punch base.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Wikipedia: Rule-based DFM analysis for deep drawing

rule_name: Punch-die clearance exceeds sheet thickness
check_description: Verify punch-to-die clearance in a deep-draw tool is greater than the nominal sheet thickness, to avoid excessive ironing/thinning, while not so large that wall wrinkling occurs.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Wikipedia: Rule-based DFM analysis for deep drawing
notes: Tooling parameter rather than a directly measurable part-geometry value; flag for process/tooling review.

rule_name: Flag high-springback bend/material combinations
check_description: Identify bends with a large radius-to-thickness ratio or in high-strength/high-temper materials, which are more prone to springback and may need over-bend compensation in tooling.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs: The Basics of Bend Radii in Sheet Metal
notes: Springback increases with material yield strength and R/T ratio; steel, aluminium and stainless behave differently and compensation is usually handled in tooling, not part geometry.

rule_name: Bend angle tolerance
check_description: Check that specified bend angle tolerances are not tighter than the shop-standard +/-1-2 degrees achievable on a press brake without secondary correction.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Sheet Metal Mini-Guide

rule_name: Hole-to-hole and edge-to-edge positional tolerance vs. thickness
check_description: Verify positional tolerance between two punched/cut features is within +/-0.13 mm (thin stock, <0.13in) to +/-0.38 mm (thick stock) as an achievable single-surface fabrication tolerance.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Sheet Metal Fabrication Design Guidelines
notes: Bend-to-bend tolerance is looser still (approx. 0.38-0.64mm) because it stacks bend-process variation.

rule_name: General profile/cutout tolerance
check_description: Check that overall cut-profile dimensions are not toleranced tighter than the process's standard cutting tolerance (approx. +/-0.5 mm) without flagging for premium or secondary processing.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Xometry Sheet Metal Mini-Guide
notes: Laser cutting alone can hold tighter (~±0.05mm per Hubs); this is a general fabrication default, not laser-specific.

rule_name: Internal vertical corner radius vs. pocket depth
check_description: For each internal pocket, verify the vertical corner radius is at least one-third of the pocket depth, since deeper pockets require proportionally larger radii to accommodate a sufficiently rigid end mill.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Pocket floor radius options
check_description: Check pocket floor corners are either left sharp (flat-bottomed, square end mill) or specified with a standard 0.5 mm or 1 mm radius, matching common tool geometries.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Internal corner radius sized slightly larger than tool radius
check_description: Verify internal fillet radii are specified marginally larger than the nearest standard end-mill radius (e.g. slightly over 3.175 mm rather than exactly 3.175 mm), so a standard tool can produce the feature without excessive deflection.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Internal corner radius must exceed half the cutter diameter
check_description: For any internal corner, check the specified radius is greater than half of the smallest standard cutter diameter that can reach the feature, since a smaller radius requires an undersized, fragile tool or EDM.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Recommended pocket depth-to-width ratio
check_description: Flag pockets where depth exceeds 4x the pocket's smallest width, since deeper cavities need longer, more deflection-prone tools that hurt accuracy and surface finish.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Feasible pocket depth relative to tool diameter
check_description: Check that pocket depth does not exceed roughly 10x the tool diameter needed to cut the pocket's internal corner radius, beyond which standard tooling cannot reliably reach the floor.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide
notes: Depths beyond this (up to ~30:1 with specialised long-reach tooling, max ~350mm) should be flagged for manual process review.

rule_name: Minimum wall thickness for metals
check_description: Check that thin-wall metal features are at least 0.8 mm thick (recommended) and never below 0.5 mm (feasible minimum), below which walls risk chatter-induced deflection or breakage during machining.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide
notes: Metal-specific (steel/aluminium/stainless); softer alloys may need a larger practical minimum.

rule_name: Minimum wall thickness for plastics
check_description: Check that thin-wall plastic features are at least 1.5 mm thick (recommended) and never below 1.0 mm (feasible minimum), since plastics deflect and heat up more readily under cutting loads.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide
notes: Plastic-specific; varies further by the stiffness of the specific polymer.

rule_name: Tall thin feature aspect ratio limit
check_description: For thin protruding walls or ribs, verify height-to-width aspect ratio stays below 4:1, to avoid vibration-induced dimensional inaccuracy and tool chatter marks.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: End-mill depth-of-cut limit varies by material
check_description: Verify pocket/slot depth machined with a given end-mill diameter does not exceed the material-dependent multiple: approx. 15xD in plastics, 10xD in aluminium, 5xD in steel, beyond which tool deflection and breakage risk rises sharply.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv CNC Machining Design Guide
notes: Material dependence: steel is most restrictive, plastics least restrictive.

rule_name: Minimum drillable hole diameter
check_description: Flag holes specified smaller than 1 mm diameter, below which standard drilling becomes unreliable and requires specialised micro-drilling.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Recommended hole depth-to-diameter ratio
check_description: Check drilled hole depth against nominal diameter: flag depths beyond 4xD (recommended limit) and treat depths beyond about 10xD as requiring special deep-hole drilling processes.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide
notes: Up to ~40xD feasible with specialised gun-drilling equipment.

rule_name: Absolute maximum drilling depth vs. bit diameter
check_description: Verify no drilled hole exceeds 12x the diameter of the nearest available standard drill bit, the practical limit before excessive bit walk and breakage risk.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Minimum and recommended thread engagement length
check_description: For tapped holes, verify thread engagement length is at least 1.5x the nominal thread diameter, with 3xD recommended for full strength in typical materials.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Unthreaded bottom clearance on blind tapped holes
check_description: Check blind tapped holes include an unthreaded clearance zone at the bottom of at least 1.5x the thread's nominal diameter, to allow for tap chamfer/runout without bottoming out.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Prefer standard thread sizes M6 or larger
check_description: Flag threaded features smaller than M6 for design review, since threads down to M2 are feasible but raise cost and breakage risk, and check thread callouts match standard metric/UNC/UNF sizes rather than custom pitches.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Minimum engraved text size
check_description: For engraved/embossed text or logos, verify character size is at least approximately 5 mm stroke height (about 20pt font) to remain legible and machinable with standard engraving tools.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Undercut/T-slot width within standard tool range
check_description: For undercut or T-slot features, verify the slot width falls within the 3-40 mm range machinable with standard T-slot/dovetail cutters.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Undercut clearance to adjacent walls
check_description: Check that the clear space between an undercut feature and any adjacent internal wall is at least 4x the undercut depth, giving the specialised cutter enough clearance to access the feature.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide
notes: Requires tool-path/accessibility simulation rather than a simple distance measurement.

rule_name: Flag features unreachable by standard-length tooling
check_description: Identify deep, narrow internal features (pockets, slots, holes) whose depth-to-access-width ratio exceeds what a standard-length tool can reach without excessive overhang, requiring custom/extended tooling or EDM.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): How to Design Parts for CNC Machining

rule_name: Default achievable dimensional tolerance
check_description: Check that toleranced dimensions are not tighter than the process default of +/-0.125 mm unless a tighter feasible tolerance (down to +/-0.025 mm) is explicitly justified, since tighter tolerances raise cost and cycle time.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
