source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Very tight tolerance cost/feasibility threshold
check_description: Flag any toleranced dimension tighter than +/-0.05 mm for manual review, since below this threshold parts may require grinding/EDM finishing beyond standard 3-axis milling capability.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Plastic tolerance practical minimum
check_description: For plastic components, flag tolerances tighter than +/-0.1 mm, since thermal expansion and machining-induced heating make sub-0.1mm tolerances impractical to hold consistently.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv CNC Machining Design Guide
notes: Material dependence: plastics only; metals can typically hold tighter tolerances (see MC-022).

rule_name: Minimise number of machine setups/orientations
check_description: Count the distinct part orientations implied by the feature set (faces requiring machining access) and flag designs needing more than 3-4 setups as adding cost, cycle time, and stack-up tolerance risk.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): CNC Machining Design Guide
notes: Requires feature-access/orientation analysis, not a single geometric measurement.

rule_name: Provide a flat, accessible workholding/reference surface
check_description: Check the part design includes at least one sizeable flat face (or added stock/tabs) usable for vice or fixture clamping without interfering with machined features.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Protolabs Network (Hubs): How to Design Parts for CNC Machining

rule_name: Turning length-to-diameter ratio limit
check_description: For turned (lathe) features, verify the unsupported length-to-diameter ratio stays at or below 8:1 to avoid chatter and deflection; ratios beyond this need steady-rest or tailstock support.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Minimum turned-wall thickness
check_description: Check that thin-walled turned features (tubes, sleeves) maintain wall thickness above approximately 0.5 mm, to preserve stiffness against cutting forces and prevent chatter or collapse.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Part envelope should align with standard stock sizes
check_description: Check overall part bounding-box dimensions against standard round/rectangular/plate stock sizes for the chosen material, flagging designs that require oversized custom billet and generate excess waste/cost.
guideline_ref: published DFM practice (fabrication design guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv CNC Machining Design Guide

rule_name: Apply Three-Question Minimum-Parts Test
check_description: For each part, an agent/human reviewer checks whether it meets at least one of the three Boothroyd DFA criteria (needs a different material/process than adjacent parts, must move relative to adjacent parts, or must remain separate for assembly/service/adjustment); parts meeting none are flagged as consolidation candidates.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: DFMA.com — Design for Assembly Principles, Examples & Checklist
notes: Core Boothroyd-Dewhurst DFA minimum-part-count criterion; requires human/agent judgment on function, not pure geometry.

rule_name: Benchmark Part Count Against Comparable Assemblies
check_description: Checker compares the total unique part count in a subassembly against historical/benchmark counts for functionally similar assemblies and flags subassemblies with disproportionately high part counts for DFA review.
typical_threshold: documented DFA redesigns achieve 30-60% typical part-count reduction (up to 83% in published case studies)
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: DFMA.com — Design for Assembly Principles, Examples & Checklist
notes: Requires an external benchmark dataset of comparable assemblies; not computable from geometry alone.

rule_name: Combine Statically-Adjacent Parts of Compatible Material/Process
check_description: Checker identifies pairs/groups of adjacent parts with no relative motion between them and flags cases where they could plausibly be molded or formed as a single part using a common material/process.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fractory — Design for Assembly (DFA) Principles Explained
notes: Consolidation candidates still require manufacturing feasibility review (mold complexity, tooling cost).

rule_name: Compute Manual Assembly Design Efficiency Index
check_description: Checker computes the Boothroyd-Dewhurst manual assembly efficiency Ema = (Nmin x ta) / tma, where Nmin is the theoretical minimum part count and ta is the 3-second ideal assembly time per part, and flags assemblies scoring well below typical benchmark efficiencies.
typical_threshold: Ema = Nmin x 3s / tma; documented redesigns improved Ema from roughly 4% to 36% (DFA Index 3.8 to 35.8 in one case study)
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: 1Library — Boothroyd-Dewhurst DFA Method (Design for Assembly)
notes: Requires assembly-time estimation (tma) not yet derivable from CAD geometry alone; formula corroborated by dfma.com case-study figures.

rule_name: Minimize Total Fastener Count
check_description: Checker counts discrete threaded/mechanical fasteners in the assembly and flags high counts as candidates for replacement with snap-fits or self-retaining features.
typical_threshold: published case studies report up to 100% fastener elimination via redesign to snap-fit/self-retaining features
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: DFMA.com — Design for Assembly Principles, Examples & Checklist

rule_name: Minimize Fastener Type and Size Variety
check_description: Checker enumerates distinct fastener types, drive styles, and sizes used across the assembly and flags high variety relative to a single-product or single-subassembly baseline.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fractory — Design for Assembly (DFA) Principles Explained
notes: No universal numeric target found in public sources; treated as a review flag rather than a hard limit.

rule_name: Prefer Snap-Fit/Self-Retaining Features Over Threaded Fasteners
check_description: Reviewer flags joints using threaded fasteners where local geometry could plausibly support a snap-fit, tab, or press-fit retention feature instead, since threaded fasteners are cited as a leading source of assembly-line defects.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fractory — Design for Assembly (DFA) Principles Explained

rule_name: Enforce Single-Direction (Top-Down) Assembly
check_description: Checker walks the assembly sequence/insertion vectors of all parts and flags any part requiring an insertion direction different from the dominant build axis, or requiring the sub-assembly to be reoriented/flipped.
typical_threshold: target = 0 reorientations; single-axis top-down assembly is the reference best-practice pattern (e.g. Sony Walkman case)
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fractory — Design for Assembly (DFA) Principles Explained
notes: Requires an assembly-sequence model, not just static geometry.

rule_name: Verify Collision-Free Insertion Path Clearance
check_description: Checker translates each mating part along its designated insertion vector and verifies no interference/clash occurs with surrounding geometry, and that minimum clearance along the path meets a specified value.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: DFMA.com — Design for Assembly Principles, Examples & Checklist
notes: Directly computable today via CAD interference/clash detection along the insertion axis; numeric clearance threshold is part/process specific.

rule_name: Provide Chamfers/Lead-Ins on Mating Features
check_description: Checker inspects pins, bosses, and mating edges for the presence of a chamfer or lead-in radius that guides insertion and reduces jamming risk.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fractory — Design for Assembly (DFA) Principles Explained
notes: Source confirms the practice qualitatively (a small chamfer can make a large difference) without a specific published numeric value; geometry is measurable once a target is set.

rule_name: Design Parts Symmetric About the Insertion Axis (or Clearly Asymmetric)
check_description: Checker evaluates each part's rotational/mirror symmetry about its insertion axis; parts should either be fully symmetric (fit either way) or have an obviously large asymmetry that prevents ambiguous orientation during assembly.
typical_threshold: fully symmetric parts (e.g. 180 degree or 360 degree rotational symmetry about the insertion axis) minimize orientation time per Boothroyd-Dewhurst orientation-time tables
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fractory — Design for Assembly (DFA) Principles Explained
notes: Rotational/mirror symmetry about a stated axis is directly computable from CAD geometry.

rule_name: Provide Self-Locating / Self-Aligning Features at Mating Interfaces
check_description: Checker verifies presence of self-locating geometry (tabs, slots, grooves, pilot diameters, locating bosses) at mating interfaces so parts align without manual fixturing.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fractory / DFMA.com — Design for Assembly

rule_name: Use Poka-Yoke Keying Features to Prevent Incorrect Assembly
check_description: Reviewer verifies asymmetric notches, keys, or datum features exist that make an incorrect assembly orientation either physically impossible or immediately visually obvious.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fractory — Design for Assembly (DFA) Principles Explained

rule_name: Flag Parts With Poor Manual/Automated Handling Characteristics
check_description: Checker flags parts that are very small relative to typical gripper/hand size, highly flexible, or prone to nesting/tangling with identical parts, all of which slow handling time.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: DFMA.com / Discover Engineering — Design for Assembly
notes: Boothroyd-Dewhurst handling-time tables quantify this via coded handling-difficulty factors not yet implemented in this checker.

rule_name: Verify Assembly Tool/Hand Access Clearance at Each Build Step
check_description: Checker verifies sufficient clearance and line-of-sight for the required tool or hand (e.g. driver, gripper) at the geometry state existing at each assembly operation, given already-installed surrounding parts.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: DFMA.com — Design for Assembly Principles, Examples & Checklist
notes: Computable via swept-volume/clash check of a tool envelope against assembly-stage geometry once tool envelopes are defined.

rule_name: Standardize Components Within and Across Product Line
check_description: Reviewer flags parts (fasteners, connectors, brackets) that are unique one-off designs where a standardized or already-used component from the same product/product line could serve the same function.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fractory / DFMA.com — Design for Assembly

rule_name: Ensure Visibility and Reachability of Service-Critical Components
check_description: Reviewer verifies components requiring regular inspection/replacement (filters, batteries, wear parts) are visible and reachable without disassembling unrelated systems.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv — Design for Serviceability

rule_name: Verify Geometric Service-Access Envelope Is Clash-Free
check_description: Checker sweeps a defined tool/hand access envelope from the nearest opening to each identified service point and verifies no interference with surrounding parts across the accessible range of motion.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv — Design for Serviceability
notes: Directly computable via CAD swept-volume/clash detection once service points and access envelopes are defined.

rule_name: Flag Awkward Service Postures
check_description: Reviewer flags service points that require the technician to lean over, reach into a confined cavity, or crawl under/over the product to perform the task.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv — Design for Serviceability

rule_name: Position Wear/Failure-Prone Components Toward Exterior
check_description: Reviewer checks that components with high expected failure/service frequency (filters, seals, batteries, fans) are located near the product's exterior/access panels rather than buried deep in the core assembly.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv — Design for Serviceability

rule_name: Use Robust Threads/Inserts on Repeatedly-Removed Interfaces
check_description: Checker verifies bosses/threads on parts intended for frequent removal (battery covers, filter housings) use metal inserts or reinforced threads rather than bare plastic threads prone to stripping.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv — Design for Serviceability

rule_name: Minimize Disassembly Depth to Reach Serviceable Components
check_description: Checker counts the number of parts/fasteners that must be removed, in sequence, to reach a given serviceable component, and flags excessive disassembly depth versus a target maximum.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv / Fusion Design Inc — Design for Serviceability
notes: Requires a disassembly-sequence model derived from the assembly tree; not yet automated in this checker.

rule_name: Require Non-Destructive Disassembly of Serviceable Joints
check_description: Reviewer verifies serviceable components can be removed without cutting, prying, or permanently deforming adjacent parts (e.g. flags ultrasonic welds or structural adhesive used over joints intended for service).
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fusion Design Inc — Designing for Serviceability Guidelines

rule_name: Isolate Service Tasks From Unrelated Subsystems
check_description: Reviewer checks that accessing a given serviceable component does not require removing unrelated subsystems (e.g. unrelated electrical harnesses or structural covers) not connected to that service task.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv — Design for Serviceability

rule_name: Partition Product Into Modular, Independently Replaceable Subassemblies
check_description: Reviewer verifies the product architecture is divided into subassemblies with clear mechanical/electrical interfaces aligned to known failure/wear points, so a module can be swapped without disturbing unrelated systems.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv — Design for Serviceability

rule_name: Key Field-Replaceable Unit Connectors to Prevent Incorrect Reassembly
check_description: Checker verifies electrical/mechanical quick-disconnect interfaces on field-replaceable units are accessible and keyed/polarized so they cannot be reconnected incorrectly.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fusion Design Inc — Designing for Serviceability Guidelines

rule_name: Use Toolless/Quick-Release Fasteners at High-Frequency Service Points
check_description: Reviewer verifies components requiring frequent service use toolless mechanisms (snap latches, quarter-turn fasteners, captive thumbscrews) rather than standard threaded fasteners requiring tools.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fusion Design Inc — Designing for Serviceability Guidelines

rule_name: Minimize Distinct Service-Tool Types Required
check_description: Checker enumerates the distinct drive types/tool sizes needed to fully service the product (open all access panels, remove all wear parts) and flags high tool variety.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fusion Design Inc — Designing for Serviceability Guidelines

rule_name: Use Captive Fasteners on Removable Access Panels
check_description: Reviewer verifies fasteners retaining removable panels/covers are captive (retained to the panel) to prevent loss during field service.
guideline_ref: published DFA/DFX practice (Boothroyd-Dewhurst and industry guides) — no ISO equivalent
source_name: Fictiv — Design for Serviceability

rule_name: Apply a Default General Tolerance Class to Untoleranced Dimensions
check_description: Checker verifies every dimension without an explicit tolerance is covered by a stated general-tolerance class (e.g. ISO 2768 fine/medium/coarse/very-coarse) appropriate to the part's process, rather than left undefined.
typical_threshold: ISO 2768 medium (m) class example: +/-0.20 mm for 6-30 mm dimensions, +/-0.30 mm for 30-120 mm dimensions
guideline_ref: ISO 2768
source_name: GEMS Manufacturing — General Tolerance Standards in Manufacturing (ISO 2768, ISO 286, GD&T)
notes: standard named, not clause-verified; exact class boundaries vary by dimension range per the standard's tables.

rule_name: Check Injection-Molded Feature Tolerances Against Process Capability
check_description: Checker compares specified tolerances on molded features against typical achievable injection-molding process tolerances for the feature's size range and flags tolerances tighter than commercial-grade capability without stated justification (e.g. fine-grade tooling, secondary machining).
typical_threshold: commercial-grade injection molding: approx +/-0.075 to 0.125 mm for 1-20 mm features; fine-grade: approx +/-0.03 to 0.08 mm for 1-20 mm features
source_name: Fictiv — The Ultimate Guide to Injection Molding Tolerances
notes: standard named, not clause-verified; source table values are industry (SPI-style) figures rather than direct ISO 20457 quotations.

rule_name: Check Sheet-Metal Bend-Angle Tolerance Against Process Capability
check_description: Checker compares specified bend-angle tolerances on sheet-metal parts against typical achievable fabrication capability and flags tolerances tighter than standard-grade capability without justification.
typical_threshold: standard sheet-metal bending: approx +/-1.0 degree; precision: approx +/-0.5 degree
guideline_ref: ISO 2768
source_name: Komacut — Sheet Metal Tolerances Guide with Charts and Standards
notes: standard named, not clause-verified; ISO 2768 covers general linear/angular tolerances applied to sheet-metal parts per source.

rule_name: Check Sheet-Metal Hole-Position Tolerance Against Process Capability
check_description: Checker compares specified hole-position tolerances on sheet-metal parts against typical achievable fabrication capability (process-dependent, e.g. laser vs. punch) and flags tolerances tighter than capability without justification.
typical_threshold: standard: approx +/-0.12 mm; precision: approx +/-0.08 mm; tight laser-cut features achievable to approx +/-0.13 mm
guideline_ref: ISO 2768
source_name: Komacut — Sheet Metal Tolerances Guide with Charts and Standards
notes: standard named, not clause-verified.

rule_name: Flag Flatness/Warpage Risk on Large Thin Molded Surfaces
check_description: Checker identifies large, thin, or unsupported molded surfaces and compares implied/specified flatness requirements against typical achievable flatness for the feature size, flagging warpage risk.
typical_threshold: typical molded flatness/straightness: approx 0.3-0.85 mm (commercial) to 0.15-0.5 mm (fine) for 0-100 mm features, looser for larger features
source_name: Fictiv — The Ultimate Guide to Injection Molding Tolerances
notes: standard named, not clause-verified.

rule_name: Assign a Defined ISO 286 Fit Class to Mating Hole/Shaft Pairs
check_description: Checker verifies every mating hole/shaft interface is assigned an explicit ISO 286 fit designation (clearance, transition, or interference) consistent with the joint's functional requirement (sliding, location, or press-fit).
typical_threshold: example clearance fit H7/h6 for sliding/bearing fits; example interference fit H7/p6 for pressed gears/pulleys; example transition fit H7/k6
guideline_ref: ISO 286
source_name: GEMS Manufacturing — General Tolerance Standards in Manufacturing (ISO 2768, ISO 286, GD&T)
notes: standard named, not clause-verified.

rule_name: Match IT Grade to Functional Precision Need
check_description: Checker verifies the IT (International Tolerance) grade assigned to a toleranced feature is no tighter than needed for its functional precision, avoiding IT grades that exceed process capability or cost targets without justification.
typical_threshold: example values at 18-30 mm nominal size: IT6 approx 10 micrometers, IT7 approx 16, IT8 approx 25, IT9 approx 40, IT10 approx 64
guideline_ref: ISO 286
source_name: GEMS Manufacturing — General Tolerance Standards in Manufacturing (ISO 2768, ISO 286, GD&T)
notes: standard named, not clause-verified.

rule_name: Apply True-Position Tolerancing to Functional/Mating Holes
check_description: Checker verifies functional or mating holes (fastener clearance holes, locating-pin holes) carry a true-position geometric callout referenced to appropriate datums, rather than relying on a plus/minus coordinate tolerance alone.
typical_threshold: illustrative example only: 0.1 mm diameter position tolerance zone commonly cited for a fastener-clearance hole; actual value is function- and fit-specific
guideline_ref: ISO 1101
source_name: GEMS Manufacturing — General Tolerance Standards in Manufacturing (ISO 2768, ISO 286, GD&T)
notes: standard named, not clause-verified; example value is illustrative, not a mandated figure.

rule_name: Apply Form/Orientation Controls to Critical Mating or Sealing Surfaces
check_description: Checker verifies flatness, perpendicularity, or parallelism controls are applied to surfaces critical to mating or sealing performance, rather than relying on size tolerance alone to control their form.
guideline_ref: ISO 1101
source_name: ISO — ISO 1101:2017, Geometrical product specifications (GPS) — Geometrical tolerancing — Tolerances of form, orientation, location and run-out
notes: standard named, not clause-verified; title confirmed via ISO.org standard listing.

rule_name: Avoid Redundant/Conflicting Size-Plus-Geometric Tolerance Callouts
check_description: Checker flags features simultaneously governed by both a plus/minus size dimension and a geometric control covering the same variation, which can create conflicting or ambiguous requirements under the fundamental tolerancing principle.
guideline_ref: ISO 8015
source_name: ISO — ISO 8015:2011, Geometrical product specifications (GPS) — Fundamentals — Concepts, principles and rules
notes: standard named, not clause-verified.

rule_name: Select Datums Based on Functional Assembly Interfaces
check_description: Reviewer verifies primary, secondary, and tertiary datums are chosen from surfaces/features that are functionally significant to the part's assembly and use (mounting face, locating hole/pin, alignment edge) and reflect the real assembly sequence, not chosen merely for measurement convenience.
guideline_ref: ISO 5459
source_name: Jiga — Datum Reference Frames (DRFs) in GD&T: Guidelines and Best Practices
notes: standard named, not clause-verified.

rule_name: Verify Datum Reference Frame Fully Constrains Six Degrees of Freedom
check_description: Checker verifies the combination of primary, secondary, and tertiary datums constrains all six degrees of freedom (3 translational, 3 rotational) without redundant or conflicting constraint, per the standard primary=3/secondary=2/tertiary=1 DOF allocation.
typical_threshold: primary datum constrains 3 DOF, secondary constrains 2 DOF, tertiary constrains 1 DOF; total = 6 DOF
guideline_ref: ISO 5459
source_name: GD&T Basics — The Datum Reference Frame
notes: standard named, not clause-verified.

rule_name: Maintain Consistent Datum Structure Across Design, Manufacturing, and Inspection
check_description: Reviewer verifies the same datum features and datum reference frame defined on the model/drawing are used for manufacturing fixturing and for inspection/CMM programming, to avoid pass-inspection-but-fails-assembly discrepancies.
guideline_ref: ISO 5459
source_name: Beska — GD&T and Tolerance Stack-Up: Improve Assembly Accuracy
notes: standard named, not clause-verified.

rule_name: Identify Critical Dimensional Chains Between Functional Surfaces
check_description: Checker traces chains of toleranced dimensions/features connecting two functionally critical surfaces (e.g. across an assembly gap, mating interface, or clearance path) and flags chains with many links or large cumulative tolerance for dedicated stack-up analysis.
guideline_ref: published dimensional-tolerancing / tolerance-stack-up practice (industry guides) — no ISO equivalent cited
source_name: Beska — GD&T and Tolerance Stack-Up: Improve Assembly Accuracy
notes: Requires an automated dimension-chain extraction capability not yet implemented in this checker.

rule_name: Select and Document Worst-Case vs. Statistical (RSS) Stack-Up Method
check_description: Reviewer verifies that, for each identified critical tolerance stack, the appropriate analysis method has been selected and documented — worst-case for safety/interference-critical stacks, statistical/RSS for high-volume manufacturing where some variation cancellation is acceptable.
guideline_ref: published dimensional-tolerancing / tolerance-stack-up practice (industry guides) — no ISO equivalent cited
source_name: Beska — GD&T and Tolerance Stack-Up: Improve Assembly Accuracy

rule_name: Concentrate Tight Tolerances on Function-Critical Features
check_description: Reviewer verifies tighter tolerances are applied only to dimensions/features that directly affect assembly fit or product function, while non-critical dimensions are left at the relaxed general-tolerance class, per functional dimensioning best practice.
guideline_ref: published dimensional-tolerancing / tolerance-stack-up practice (industry guides) — no ISO equivalent cited
source_name: Beska — GD&T and Tolerance Stack-Up: Improve Assembly Accuracy

rule_name: Enclosure openings must reject the IP2X jointed test finger (Probe B)
check_description: No opening path in the enclosure geometry should admit the IEC 61032 Probe B jointed-finger envelope (12mm dia segment, 80mm knurled length, two pivot joints bending up to 90 deg, 50mm x 20mm baffle stop) to reach live/hazardous internal parts.
typical_threshold: Knurled finger dia 12mm +/-0.1mm, length 80mm +/-0.2mm; baffle plate 50mm dia x 20mm thick; 2 pivot joints, max bend 90 +/-10 deg; total probe length 300mm +/-0.5mm; applied force 10N +/-0.5N (public product-spec summary of IEC 61032 Probe B)
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes) / IEC 60529 (IP code) / IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
source_name: LISUN - Test Probe B of IEC 61032 (Jointed Test Finger)
notes: Dimensions above come from a test-equipment vendor's public product page summarizing the probe geometry, not from the IEC 61032 primary text. A human must verify exact probe geometry, articulation rules, and applicable pass/fail criteria against the purchased IEC 61032 and relevant IEC 60335-1 clause before use. Simulating full articulated-probe path search against arbitrary 3D geometry is algorithmically hard; current pipeline can only flag opening bounding dimensions, not certify full accessibility.

rule_name: IP1X-level openings must reject 50mm back-of-hand test sphere
check_description: No opening should allow a 50mm-diameter rigid sphere (back-of-hand surrogate) to pass through to a hazard, for the lowest IP first-digit protection tier.
typical_threshold: 50 mm sphere / 'hand-sized' object exclusion (IP1X, public secondary summary of IEC 60529)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
source_name: China-Gauges - Understanding IP Code Ratings: A Guide to IEC 60529 Compliance
notes: This is a secondary-source restatement of the IEC 60529 first-digit table, not the primary standard text; a human must confirm exact object/probe geometry (test sphere vs other described object) and confirm the appliance's declared IP first digit against the purchased IEC 60529 before treating 50mm as a hard pass/fail gate.

rule_name: IP3X-level openings must reject 2.5mm tool/wire probe
check_description: No opening should allow a 2.5mm-diameter rigid probe (representing tools/wires) to reach hazardous internal parts, for IP first-digit level 3 enclosures.
typical_threshold: 2.5 mm probe exclusion (IP3X, public secondary summary of IEC 60529)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
source_name: China-Gauges - Understanding IP Code Ratings: A Guide to IEC 60529 Compliance
notes: Value is from a secondary compliance-vendor summary, not the primary IEC 60529 text. Human must verify the exact probe geometry (rigid straight probe vs jointed finger) and confirm which IP first digit applies to the specific product zone before use.

rule_name: IP4X-level openings must reject 1.0mm fine wire probe
check_description: No opening should allow a 1.0mm-diameter rigid wire probe to reach hazardous internal parts, for IP first-digit level 4 enclosures (finest openings before dust-protection tiers).
typical_threshold: 1.0 mm probe exclusion (IP4X, public secondary summary of IEC 60529)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
source_name: China-Gauges - Understanding IP Code Ratings: A Guide to IEC 60529 Compliance
notes: Secondary-source value; a human must verify against purchased IEC 60529 primary text and confirm which enclosure zones require IP4X vs a lower tier.

rule_name: Straight rigid test pin check for slots with unobstructed line-of-sight to hazard
check_description: For slot/vent geometries with a straight, unobstructed line-of-sight path to a live or hazardous part, verify the minimum cross-section rejects the applicable rigid test probe diameter (no articulation needed for a straight-through path).
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes) / IEC 60529 (IP code)
notes: This is a reasonable engineering inference (straight-path slots are the simplest case of the general probe-access rule) but no specific public source was fetched for this exact framing. A human must verify against IEC 61032/60529 primary text and confirm whether the applicable geometry is genuinely straight-line (no need for articulated-probe simulation) before relying on a simplified rigid-pin check.

rule_name: Enclosure seams/vents must not present a direct path for vertically falling drops (IPX1)
check_description: Verify that any top-facing opening, seam, or vent does not create a straight vertical path from outside to internal electrical parts, for the lowest IP second-digit (dripproof) tier.
typical_threshold: Protection against vertically falling water drops (IPX1, public secondary summary of IEC 60529)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
source_name: China-Gauges - Understanding IP Code Ratings: A Guide to IEC 60529 Compliance
notes: Qualitative restatement of a secondary source; a human must verify the actual IPX1 test rig geometry and drip rate against the primary IEC 60529 standard, and confirm which internal zones require this protection.

rule_name: Enclosure geometry must tolerate 15-degree tilted drop ingress (IPX2)
check_description: Verify sealed seams/openings remain protected when the product is modeled tilted up to 15 degrees from its normal drip-test orientation, per the IP second-digit level 2 tier.
typical_threshold: 15 degrees tilt (IPX2, public secondary summary of IEC 60529)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
source_name: China-Gauges - Understanding IP Code Ratings: A Guide to IEC 60529 Compliance
notes: Secondary-source restatement; a human must confirm the exact tilt test procedure and applicability against the primary IEC 60529 text before using 15 degrees as a modeling parameter.

rule_name: Vents/seams must reject 60-degree angled spray (IPX3) without direct path to live parts
check_description: Verify that any external opening does not present a direct unobstructed path to hazardous internal parts when water is modeled arriving at up to 60 degrees from vertical, for IPX3-rated zones.
typical_threshold: Spray up to 60 degrees from vertical (IPX3, public secondary summary of IEC 60529)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
source_name: China-Gauges - Understanding IP Code Ratings: A Guide to IEC 60529 Compliance
notes: Full geometric ingress-path simulation for angled spray is not yet implemented in this pipeline; flagged as a design-review item. A human must verify against the primary IEC 60529 test method and the product's declared IPX3 (or higher) rating.

rule_name: Splash-protected geometry must block ingress from any direction (IPX4)
check_description: Verify enclosure seams and openings have no direct line-of-sight path to hazardous internal parts from any azimuth/elevation angle, for IPX4-rated splashproof zones (e.g. wet-area vacuum/appliance housings).
typical_threshold: Splashing water from any direction (IPX4, public secondary summary of IEC 60529)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
source_name: China-Gauges - Understanding IP Code Ratings: A Guide to IEC 60529 Compliance
notes: Qualitative secondary-source restatement; a human must verify actual IPX4 oscillating-spray test geometry and confirm which product zones (e.g. handheld/floor-care heads used near water) require this rating against the primary standard.

rule_name: Jet-resistant seals must withstand a 6.3mm nozzle jet without ingress path (IPX5)
check_description: Verify that seam/vent gap geometry does not admit a modeled 6.3mm-diameter directed water jet to hazardous internal parts, for IPX5-rated zones.
typical_threshold: 6.3 mm nozzle diameter reference (IPX5, public secondary summary of IEC 60529)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
source_name: China-Gauges - Understanding IP Code Ratings: A Guide to IEC 60529 Compliance
notes: Nozzle diameter is a test-rig parameter, not directly a pass/fail opening-size threshold; a human must verify actual IPX5 test distance/pressure/duration and derive any geometric proxy carefully against the primary IEC 60529 text before automating this check.

rule_name: Immersion-rated housings must locate all seams/vents above or sealed below the specified test depth (IPX7)
check_description: Verify that for IPX7-rated products, any non-fully-sealed seam, button boot, or vent is either watertight or positioned/rated for the 1m/30min immersion envelope.
typical_threshold: Immersion up to 1 m for 30 minutes (IPX7, public secondary summary of IEC 60529)
guideline_ref: IEC 60529 (IP code)
source_name: China-Gauges - Understanding IP Code Ratings: A Guide to IEC 60529 Compliance
notes: Secondary-source restatement; a human must verify actual IPX7 depth/duration tolerance and applicable product classification against the primary IEC 60529 standard, especially if the product is only rated IPX4-IPX6 rather than IPX7.

rule_name: Small square/rectangular openings require minimum hazard-zone setback distance
check_description: For a square opening with side length between roughly 12mm and 20mm, verify the internal hazard (e.g. rotating brush roll, blade) is set back at least the published minimum distance from the opening plane.
typical_threshold: Opening side 12-20 mm requires hazard zone >=120 mm away (worked example, public summary of ISO 13857 Table 4/5)
guideline_ref: ISO 13857 (safety distances)
source_name: GT Engineering - EN ISO 13857 Safety Distances to Prevent Access by Upper Limbs
notes: This is a single worked example from a secondary engineering-consultancy page illustrating one row of the ISO 13857 opening-vs-distance tables; the full table (all opening size bands and both adult/child cases) is in the paywalled primary standard and was not verified here. A human must obtain the primary ISO 13857 Table 4 (14+ years) and Table 5 (3+ years) before applying this as a general rule across all opening sizes.

rule_name: Safety distances must account for both adult (14+) and child (3+) reach-through geometry
check_description: Verify hazard setback distances are checked against two separate anthropometric population cases where a product may be accessible to children: the general (14 years and older, 95th percentile) case and the supplementary child (3 years and older) case for reaching through openings.
guideline_ref: ISO 13857 (safety distances)
source_name: ISO.org - ISO 13857:2019 Safety of machinery - Safety distances
notes: Scope confirmed from the ISO.org standard abstract page only (population coverage and general intent); the actual distance tables and geometric limb models are in the primary paywalled standard and were not accessed. A human must verify which population case(s) apply to the specific Dyson product (e.g. household appliances reasonably accessible to children) and pull exact table values from the purchased standard.

rule_name: Reach-over protective structure height/depth combination must exceed hazard access envelope
check_description: For guards or housings that a user could reach over (e.g. top of a tall appliance) rather than through an opening, verify the combination of barrier height and horizontal distance to the hazard exceeds the reach-over envelope defined by ISO 13857.
guideline_ref: ISO 13857 (safety distances)
source_name: ISO.org - ISO 13857:2019 Safety of machinery - Safety distances
notes: Only the standard's existence and general scope were verified from the public abstract; the reach-over height/distance table values were not accessed (primary standard is paywalled). A human must obtain the primary ISO 13857 reach-over table before setting numeric thresholds; this pipeline cannot yet run full limb-reach envelope geometry.

rule_name: Reach-under gaps beneath the product must impede lower-limb access to hazards
check_description: Verify that any gap beneath a floor-standing or countertop appliance through which a foot or leg could reach is either too small or positioned far enough from moving/hot/live parts, per ISO 13857 lower-limb guidance.
guideline_ref: ISO 13857 (safety distances)
source_name: ISO.org - ISO 13857:2019 Safety of machinery - Safety distances
notes: General coverage of lower-limb access is confirmed in the ISO.org abstract; exact gap/distance numeric values require the primary standard, which was not accessed. A human must verify applicability to Dyson floor-care/stand-mounted products and confirm exact table values.

rule_name: Minimum creepage path length along insulation surfaces between live conductors
check_description: Verify the shortest path measured along the surface of solid insulation between two conductors at different potentials meets or exceeds the minimum required for the working voltage, pollution degree, and material CTI group; ribs/grooves may be needed to lengthen the surface path within the same footprint.
guideline_ref: IEC 60664-1 (insulation coordination / creepage & clearance)
source_name: In Compliance Magazine - Creepage Distance
notes: Only the qualitative definition and the dependency on voltage/CTI/pollution degree were confirmed from a public explainer; the actual minimum-distance lookup tables are in the primary IEC 60664-1 standard and were not accessed. This check also requires electrical inputs (working voltage, insulation class, CTI of actual material) that are outside pure geometry and must be supplied by electrical engineering before a human can verify compliance.

rule_name: Minimum through-air clearance between conductors at different potentials
check_description: Verify the shortest straight-line (through-air) distance between two conductors at different potentials meets or exceeds the minimum required for the working voltage and overvoltage category.
guideline_ref: IEC 60664-1 (insulation coordination / creepage & clearance)
source_name: In Compliance Magazine - Creepage Distance
notes: Qualitative definition confirmed from a public explainer only; numeric minimum-clearance tables are in the primary IEC 60664-1 standard and were not accessed. Requires electrical voltage/overvoltage-category inputs from outside the geometry model; a human must verify against the primary standard and actual circuit design before sign-off.

rule_name: Insulation surface routing (ribs/grooves) used to increase effective creepage path without increasing footprint
check_description: Where direct creepage distance is insufficient within the available footprint, verify that ribs, grooves, or barrier walls are modeled to increase the effective along-surface path length between conductors.
guideline_ref: IEC 60664-1 (insulation coordination / creepage & clearance)
notes: This is standard electrical-enclosure design practice known generally, but no specific public page was fetched describing rib/groove creepage-extension rules in this exact framing. A human must verify the rules for counting rib/groove contributions to creepage distance against the primary IEC 60664-1 standard (there are specific rules about minimum rib width/height to count).

rule_name: Guard/vent openings near moving parts must combine probe-rejection and setback-distance rules
check_description: For any guard, grille, or vent adjacent to a moving hazard (e.g. brush roll, fan, gears), verify the opening simultaneously rejects the applicable IEC 61032 test probe AND, where the probe geometry alone is insufficient, provides the ISO 13857 minimum setback distance from the opening to the hazard.
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes) / ISO 13857 (safety distances) / IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
notes: This combined-check framing is a reasonable synthesis of two standards' intents but was not found verbatim on a public page; a human must verify against the primary IEC 60335-1 clauses that reference test-probe access to moving parts, and confirm whether ISO 13857 setback distances or IEC 61032 probe rejection (or both) apply to the specific moving-part hazard in question.

rule_name: Rotating-part guard slot width must remain smaller than the probe/finger geometry it must reject
check_description: Verify slot widths in guards over rotating parts (e.g. brush-bar covers, fan grilles) are dimensioned below the rejection threshold for the applicable IP first-digit/IEC 61032 probe, independent of the setback-distance rule.
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes) / IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
notes: General engineering inference from IP-code/probe principles, not tied to a specific fetched clause. A human must verify the applicable IP first digit / probe type for guards over specific moving parts (brush rolls, fans, gear trains) against the primary IEC 60335-1 and IEC 61032 texts.

rule_name: Handheld/grip surfaces require material and geometry flag for touch-temperature review
check_description: Flag any user-touched surface (handle, trigger, grip) that is within a defined proximity of a heat-generating component (motor, battery, heater element) for touch-temperature engineering review; geometry alone cannot certify compliance without material and thermal simulation data.
guideline_ref: IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
notes: No public page with specific numeric touchable-surface temperature limits (by material class) was fetched for this task; such limits exist in IEC 60335-1 Part 1/Part 2 tables and are paywalled. A human must verify applicable temperature limits by material/contact-duration class against the primary standard before treating this as more than a design-review flag.

rule_name: Externally accessible surfaces near heat sources require setback or shielding geometry
check_description: Verify externally accessible enclosure surfaces near a heat source (e.g. dryer barrel, motor housing) either maintain a minimum standoff distance or include a shielding/venting geometry, pending thermal simulation to confirm surface temperature stays within the applicable touch-temperature class.
guideline_ref: IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
notes: General inference, not sourced from a fetched public page with numeric limits. A human must verify against the primary IEC 60335-1 (and relevant Part 2 product-specific standard) touch-temperature tables and confirm this geometry-only proxy is an adequate stand-in for full thermal analysis.

rule_name: Full articulated-probe accessibility simulation is flagged as not yet computable
check_description: Record that a true geometric simulation of the IEC 61032 jointed test finger's reachable envelope through complex, multi-surface enclosure openings (accounting for all articulation angles and insertion paths) is not implemented in the current automated checker and requires either simplified bounding-geometry proxies or manual physical probe testing.
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes)
source_name: LISUN - Test Probe B of IEC 61032 (Jointed Test Finger)
notes: This row documents a known capability gap rather than a numeric rule. A human reviewer must confirm which openings require physical probe testing versus which can be cleared by simplified geometric proxies (e.g. worst-case straight-line probe diameter), and must verify against the primary IEC 61032 standard.

rule_name: Openings with re-entrant or non-convex geometry require manual probe-path review
check_description: Flag any enclosure opening whose internal geometry is non-convex (e.g. has internal pockets, undercuts, or multiple connected cavities) for manual jointed-probe accessibility review, since automated straight-line/bounding-box checks are unreliable for such shapes.
guideline_ref: IEC 61032 (test probes)
notes: This is a pragmatic engineering-review heuristic, not sourced from a specific fetched page. A human must confirm this flag correctly captures the cases where automated checks are unreliable and must still perform (or commission) the applicable physical or simulated probe test per the primary IEC 61032/60529 standards.

rule_name: Large plastic components should reserve a marking area for generic material identification
check_description: Where product-specific marking requirements apply, verify major plastic parts include a legible, accessible surface area (boss, flat, or recess) for a molded-in or applied material identification mark; ISO 11469 leaves exact size/location to manufacturer agreement rather than prescribing a universal dimension.
guideline_ref: ISO 11469 / ISO 1043 (plastics marking)
source_name: GlobalSpec - ISO 11469: Plastics - Generic identification and marking of plastics products
notes: The primary ISO 11469 standard explicitly states minimum item size, lettering size, and marking location are 'subject to agreement between manufacturer and user' rather than fixed by the standard itself, so no universal numeric threshold exists publicly. A human must confirm Dyson's internal marking specification (if any) and verify against the purchased ISO 11469/ISO 1043 texts.

rule_name: Material identification symbol must use standard ISO 1043 abbreviations where marking is applied
check_description: Where a part is marked per ISO 11469, verify the symbol used is a valid abbreviated term/symbol from the ISO 1043 series (basic polymers, fillers, plasticizers, flame retardants) rather than a free-text or proprietary code.
guideline_ref: ISO 11469 / ISO 1043 (plastics marking)
source_name: GlobalSpec - ISO 11469: Plastics - Generic identification and marking of plastics products
notes: Confirmed only at the level of 'ISO 11469 references ISO 1043 symbols' from a secondary standards-catalog summary; exact symbol syntax rules are in the primary ISO 1043 series and were not accessed. A human must verify exact symbol format against the primary standards before use in any automated marking check.

rule_name: Fasteners and joints intended for end-of-life disassembly must remain tool-accessible
check_description: Verify that fasteners/joints identified as disassembly points (for material separation or repair) have unobstructed tool access geometry (clearance for driver/tool head and swing arc) rather than being trapped behind non-removable co-molded or bonded features.
guideline_ref: IEC 62430 (ecodesign)
source_name: NEMA - ANSI/IEC 62430-2010 Contents and Scope (Environmentally Conscious Design)
notes: IEC 62430 is confirmed (from a public scope summary) to be a process-based framework requiring lifecycle/end-of-life consideration, but it does not itself prescribe numeric tool-clearance geometry. A human must verify this check against Dyson's own disassembly/repairability design guidelines and the primary IEC 62430 text, since the standard defers specifics to sector/company-level guidance.

rule_name: Product design must undergo an environmentally-conscious design (ECD) checkpoint gate before geometry freeze
check_description: Record whether the design has passed a documented environmental-aspect review (materials, disassembly, recyclability, lifecycle impacts) consistent with the IEC 62430 process stages, as a qualitative gate rather than a geometric measurement.
guideline_ref: IEC 62430 (ecodesign)
source_name: NEMA - ANSI/IEC 62430-2010 Contents and Scope (Environmentally Conscious Design)
notes: IEC 62430 is a process/management-system standard, not a source of geometric thresholds; this row is included so the checklist captures the qualitative gate. A human must confirm Dyson's internal ECD process satisfies the primary IEC 62430 requirements; no numeric geometry check applies here.

rule_name: Energy-source safeguard separation must reflect IEC 62368-1 hazard-based classification
check_description: For products with ICT/AV-adjacent subsystems (e.g. connected appliance electronics), verify that physical separation/safeguard geometry between a classified energy source (electrical, mechanical, thermal) and an ordinary person corresponds to the hazard-based safeguard approach, rather than assuming a single fixed clearance for all energy types.
source_name: Nemko - A 2-Minute Guide to the New ICT/AV Standard (IEC 62368-1)
notes: Only the hazard-based safety engineering concept and general scope (equipment covered by former IEC 60950-1/60065) were confirmed from a public explainer; the standard's energy-source class definitions and specific safeguard distance tables were not accessed and are in the paywalled primary text. A human must verify whether IEC 62368-1 (vs IEC 60335-1) is the governing standard for the specific Dyson subsystem before applying this row, and pull exact values from the primary standard.

rule_name: Household appliance enclosures must prevent probe access to both live parts and moving parts
check_description: Verify enclosure/guard openings are checked against test-probe accessibility rules for two separate hazard classes identified in IEC 60335-1: live electrical parts and moving mechanical parts, since acceptance criteria/probe types can differ between the two.
guideline_ref: IEC 60335-1 (household appliance safety) - clause not verified against primary source
source_name: UL Solutions - IEC 60335-1: the Standard for the Safety of Household and Similar Electrical Appliances
notes: Confirmed from a public UL summary that the 6th edition of IEC 60335-1 added test-probe requirements for 'access to live parts and moving parts' as two named concerns; exact clause numbers, probe types, and pass criteria were not accessed (primary standard is paywalled). A human must verify the specific clauses and probe requirements against the purchased IEC 60335-1 before use.
